issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release §5.7.8 round([precision : Integer]) : Decimal
issues.evidence: Spec says round() returns Decimal and the optional precision defaults to 0. Fresh native and forced Python fallback probe showed 1.round().type().name -> Integer, 1.round() is Decimal -> false, and 1.round() is Integer -> true, while 1.round(0).type().name -> Decimal. Reproducer: python3 .temp/qa/fp11_historian_probe.py.
issues.root_cause: Both math backends special-cased omitted round() precision by returning an Integer, even though the spec return type is Decimal and omitted precision is equivalent to precision 0.
issues.resolution: Changed Python rround() and native C++ fn_round() to always materialize Decimal output for round(), including omitted precision. Added native/fallback parity and native sqllogictest coverage for round() type/is behavior.
